newsitem.title: FRANCE: France announces 20 bln Ffr state rescue for GAN.
newsitem.headline: France announces 20 bln Ffr state rescue for GAN.

text.p: The French government, stepping in with another big rescue in the financial sector, has pledged 20 billion francs ($3.5 billion) to state-controlled insurer GAN to shore up its accounts and pave the way for its early privatisation, the company announced on Thursday.
Some 11 billion francs of the aid would come in the form of a capital injection while nine billion francs would be to cover estimated losses, Groupe des Assurances Nationales said in a statement.

"In light of the deterioration in GAN's financial situation and in its role as majority shareholder, the state has decided to give its help in the framework of a restructuring aimed at priviatising CIC and the insurance activities of GAN," GAN said.

GAN, whose woes stem mainly from its UIC property lending unit which has been hard hit by a long-running real estate slump, said it expected to post a net attributable loss of five billion francs for 1996.

That comes on top of GAN's loss of 1.79 billion francs in 1995 and a loss of 5.34 billion francs the previous year. The insurer's accounts have been gouged by provisions for troubles at its UIC property financing unit.
UIC said its net attributable losses for 1996 should total 7.9 billion francs. GAN, which is majority shareholder of UIC, plans a 7.1 billion franc recapitalisation of UIC.
GAN said in the statement the cost of its property banking losses totalled nearly 30 billion francs over three years.

Finance Minister Jean Arthuis told a news conference that the government planned to privatise GAN and along with its regional banking subsidiary Credit Industriel et Commercial (CIC) "during the course of 1997."
The government has long wanted to privatise GAN but the project has been complicated by failure of a tender last year to first sell off CIC, a profitable group of 13 regional banks.
It cancelled the tender for a trade sale in November after receiving just two offers, of which only one -- from BNP bank -- was judged eligible by France's independent Privatisation Commission.
Share trading in GAN and UIC property arm was suspended on the Paris stock exchange on Thursday. About 20 percent of GAN's shares are traded on the stock exchange.
Announcement of GAN's rescue coincides with analysts' expectations the government will pump up to 15 billion francs into state bank Credit Lyonnais to pave the way for its privatisation.
The bank, which also was hard hit by the collapse of the French property market after a reckless lending spree, has already received billions of francs in state aid.

The European Commission, which vets state help to industry in the European Union, approved a state injection of 2.9 billion francs into GAN last year and said recently that any new aid would require fresh investigation.
GAN's shares, which many analysts have now relegated to the status of a speculative stock, last traded at 123.0 francs.

The company issued a statement on February 14 to counter a recent rise in its stock price fuelled by market speculation that it could be a bid target in financial sector consolidation following the giant merger of insurers Axa and UAP.
Shares plunged after the company said the recent rise was not justified by its financial situation.
